title: Addressing Prediction Delays in Time Series Forecasting: A Continuous GRU Approach with Derivative Regularization

problem.claim: MSE-based time series forecasting can produce prediction delay, where predictions follow the ground truth and therefore may be practically meaningless.

gap.claim: Traditional time series forecasting tasks need a solution that mitigates prediction delay.

contributions.claim: Introduces a continuous-time GRU based on a neural ordinary differential equation that can supervise explicit time derivatives.
Generalizes the GRU architecture to continuous time and applies time-derivative regularization to minimize prediction delay.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper explicitly presents a new perspective on traditional time series forecasting tasks and a new solution for mitigating prediction delay.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The method reportedly outperforms in MSE, Dynamic Time Warping, and Time Distortion Index metrics.
The authors report low prediction delay across a variety of datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time series forecasting is used across application areas including economics and meteorology.
MSE is widely used, but MSE-based training can cause prediction delay that undermines practical usefulness.
The paper proposes a new perspective and introduces a continuous-time GRU with explicit time-derivative supervision.
Continuous-time GRU generalization and time-derivative regularization are used to reduce prediction delay.
The authors report improved metrics and low prediction delay across multiple datasets.
